items.title: Beyond religion and atheism: The secret third answer to big questions
items.description:
For decades, atheists have used one move to dismantle the case for God: swap in an evil one and show that the arguments work just as well. Philosopher Jack Symes was convinced by it, and was 50,000 words into a book defending atheism when he noticed that the exercise kept tipping toward goodness. He threw out the manuscript and started over. 
 
 This video  Beyond religion and atheism: The secret third answer to big questions  is featured on  Big Think .

items.title: The theory that connects the origin of life to the rise of intelligence
items.description:
From von Neumann’s blueprint, which predated the discovery of DNA, to viral genes that now help form our memories and placentas, Blaise Agüera y Arcas argues that function defines life more than material does, and that AI belongs in the same story. He explains why he thinks AGI is already here, and gives a blueprint for using AI without sacrificing your own mind. 
 This video  The theory that connects the origin of life to the rise of intelligence  is featured on  Big Think .

items.title: The hidden mass extinction happening inside your body
items.description:
There’s a mass extinction happening inside your body. Dr. Martin Blaser is a physician and microbiologist who has spent over 30 years studying the microbes that live on and in us. He’s also the author of “Missing Microbes” and co-author of the 2025 paper “The Invisible Extinction.”  
 
 This video  The hidden mass extinction happening inside your body  is featured on  Big Think .

items.title: Mercury lost its crown, and isn’t our Solar System’s hottest planet
items.description: In terms of power, the only body of note in the Solar System is the Sun. Planets, in general, reflect, absorb, and re-radiate energy emitted by their parent stars, and the Sun is the only parent star any of the planets have here in our Solar System. To an excellent approximation, the Sun keeps not only Earth, but all the planets at a temperature well above what they’d be without it, which is just a few Kelvin.
